item.title: VNtyper 2
item.description: Abstract Background: ADTKD-MUC1 is one of the major entities of ADTKD caused by frameshift variants in the MUC1 VNTR that standard short-read sequencing fails to detect. Existing 59dupC-targeted probe-extension assays do not allow for broad screening and cannot detect atypical non-dupC variants. Recently, VNtyper, a Kestrel-based genotyping pipeline with optional code-adVNTR cross-validation for MUC1 VNTR genotyping from short-read sequencing data allowed to circumvent this diagnostic limitation, but needed further development for easy access and rapid sample processing.

item.title: A tool to genotype coding VNTR in ADTKD-MUC1
item.description: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease (ADTKD) is a hereditary condition characterized by progressive tubulointerstitial fibrosis with or without tubular dilation and atrophy, eventually leading to end-stage kidney failure. The affected individuals present mild to negative proteinuria, and bland urinary sediment abnormalities, with normal kidney size. A positive family history is commonly reported for this disease. Molecular genetics play a key role in diagnosing and classifying ADTKD given their non-specific presentations. Pathogenic variants in different genes, including MUC1, UMOD, HNF1B, REN, and SEC61A1, are known to be responsible for ADTKD.
